summary: A command that checks a course and prints the report. internal/cli/check.go is hand-authored: check <a11y|dates|placeholders|links|all> with --course and --closures. It builds a course snapshot (coursesnapshot.Build, from link-pagination), hands it to cb-checks on stdin, and writes cb-checks' stdout back out byte for byte. The helper is run as `checks_command... <name> --snapshot - --closures <csv> --local-host <host:port>` under a ten-minute limit. root.go gains the AddCommand line in the hand-authored block, and the command carries a pp:path annotation of /api/v1/courses/{course_id} so Canvas Builder's untraceable-command hiding (sandbox-command-surface) keeps it visible by rule. internal/sandbox/messages.go gains MsgChecksTimeout and ChecksFailed(detail). In Canvas Builder the course, the closure days and the checks command all come from the course workspace, and the local host is the gateway's own host:port; outside it, --course and --closures are the caller's, checks_command comes from config.toml, and the local host is the Canvas base URL's host.
reason:
The checks are the only thing in this system that says whether a course is in good shape, and they live in canvas-builder-v2, not here. This command's whole job is the handover, so it is written to add nothing of its own to either side of it.

The report is passed through untouched, not parsed and reprinted. The instructor sees the same report in Canvas Builder that the agent saw; a report this CLI had reshaped on the way past would be a second, quieter opinion nobody asked for, and the first thing to drift when cb-checks grows a field. The only thing the command asks of the report is that it be JSON: checks that end well and print something else have failed without noticing, and handing that on would give the agent a report it can't read with nothing saying why.

The snapshot goes in on stdin. It is the whole of a course's text, which is far too much for a command line, and a course's content has no business appearing in a process listing.

The check's name is read before anything else. A misspelled check is a typo, and no course should be read to find that out. The same reasoning puts the missing-checks_command and the --closures refusal ahead of the snapshot: nothing can be done with a snapshot nothing will read.

In Canvas Builder the closure days come from the course workspace and --closures is refused, because the instructor entered those days in Canvas Builder and an agent passing its own list would be checking the course against a term nobody agreed to.
known_limitations:
A deliberate deviation from Plan E. The plan says a nil ClosureDays gives MsgNoClosureDays and exit 10; this refuses only when the run includes the date check, so `check dates` and `check all` stop and `check a11y`, `check placeholders` and `check links` run. Closure days are the date check's business, MsgNoClosureDays says so in as many words ("the date check didn't run"), and a course whose instructor hasn't entered them yet can still be checked for accessibility. An empty list is an answer -- this course closes on no days -- and only a missing one isn't.

--closures is always passed, with an empty value when there is nothing to pass. cb-checks reads an empty value as no closure days, so the shape of the command line is the same whichever check runs.

The report is held in memory before it is written, because it has to be JSON before any of it is printed. A report is a few kilobytes and this is not a stream.

The ten-minute limit is on one run of the checks, measured from the moment the helper starts, and the snapshot's own reads are outside it. A course slow enough to matter will be stopped by the client's own timeouts first.

When the checks fail, the message carries the first line of their stderr and nothing more. A stack trace belongs in the checks' own output, not in an agent's error. When there is no stderr at all the detail is "they produced no report."

--dry-run reports what would have been checked and stops without building a snapshot. The checks only read, so there is nothing for a dry run to hold back, but --dry-run makes every read answer "not sent" and a snapshot of those answers is a snapshot of nothing.

check does not appear in `which` yet. whichIndex is generated and the curated capability index is Task 11's work, so for now the command is found through --help.

A course with no time zone fails as an API error (exit 5) rather than a config error, because coursesnapshot.Build reports it as an ordinary error and classifyAPIError's default is exit 5. The message is still MsgNoTimeZone, which says what to do.
validated_outcome:
go build ./... clean. go test ./... passing across every package on darwin/arm64 with Go 1.27.1, exit 0. go test -race -run Check ./internal/cli/ passing. golangci-lint run --max-issues-per-linter=0 --max-same-issues=0 reports nothing on internal/cli/check.go or internal/cli/check_test.go and 0 issues on internal/sandbox; the touched generated file reports only its pre-existing findings. gofmt -l clean on every hand-authored file in this patch.

New coverage, all through runCLI against the gateway fake, with TestHelperChecks standing in for cb-checks: this test binary is handed to the command as its checks_command, so what the stand-in records is exactly what the real cb-checks would have been given. TestCheckPassesSnapshotAndClosures asserts the argv after -- is exactly `dates --snapshot - --closures 2027-05-06,2027-05-31 --local-host 127.0.0.1:<port>`, that the snapshot on stdin is of the workspace's course 7 and carries its page, and that stdout is the report byte for byte. TestCheckAllPassesThrough does the same for a four-report answer. TestCheckNeedsClosureDays covers all three cases: no closure days with `check dates` is exit 10 with MsgNoClosureDays and the checks never run, no closure days with `check a11y` runs with an empty --closures, and an empty list runs with an empty --closures. TestCheckRefusesClosuresFlagInSandbox asserts exit 2 with MsgClosuresFromWorkspace and nothing asked of Canvas. TestCheckMissingHelper asserts exit 10 with MsgChecksMissing and nothing asked of Canvas. TestCheckHelperFailure covers a non-zero exit, a clean exit printing something that isn't a report, and a failure with no stderr at all; each is exit 1 carrying the first line of stderr and nothing after it, with empty stdout. TestCheckStopsALongRun shortens checksTimeLimit to 50ms against a helper that sleeps, and asserts exit 1 with MsgChecksTimeout and nothing printed. TestCheckUnknownName asserts exit 2 naming both what was asked for and what there is, with nothing asked of Canvas. TestCheckGatewayRefusalSurfaced answers the course read with 423 and the quarantine message, and asserts exit 9 carrying Canvas Builder's own words with the checks never run. TestCheckOutsideCanvasBuilder covers the plain CLI: --course and --closures passed through with the local host taken from the base URL, a missing --course as exit 2, and a missing checks_command as exit 10. TestCheckRealHelper runs the whole handover against the real cb-checks from canvas-builder-v2 (skipped without CANVAS_BUILDER_V2 and node): a page body containing [Check: room number] gives a placeholders report with exactly one issue. Run against canvas-builder-v2 at 678f8a4 on node v22.23.3, it passes.

CodeRabbit reviewed the patch (uncommitted plus untracked, all four files) and raised two findings. One minor and valid, fixed: exec.CommandContext kills only the direct child, so if checks_command is a launcher rather than cb-checks itself, a grandchild still holding the output pipes would keep Run waiting past the ten-minute limit. helper.WaitDelay is now 5 seconds, which closes the pipes and returns. One major and wrong, skipped: it reported c.Sandbox, sandbox.ReadWorkspace and c.Config.ChecksCommand as undeclared, which they are not -- they are in internal/client/client.go, internal/sandbox/workspace.go and internal/config/config.go, all outside the reviewed diff, and go build ./... and the full test suite pass.
